answer: Verify each voting seat by postcard. The operator gives a street address, and the network mails a card printed with a one-time cipher that must be typed back within 30 days. Every address backs only one seat and is checked against the postal database, so a single harbor warehouse cannot claim a thousand units. A farmer wanting 1,000 fake seats must rent 1,000 real mailboxes at about $15 a month, $15,000 monthly, and each seat stays rooted like a vine to one place an auditor can visit.
